records.issue_text: embed.js:7 `discourseUrl + "embed/best"` assumes a trailing slash on `discourseUrl`, producing `hostembed/best` without it
records.rationale: The new embed.js line does string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. If the site owner configures discourseUrl without a trailing slash (e.g. "https://forum.example.com"), the resulting URL becomes "...comembed/best" and the embed breaks. The diff contains no normalization of discourseUrl, so the described mechanism is directly verifiable in the code; severity depends on the (external) documentation convention for discourseUrl.

records.issue_text: Migrations create_top_topics.rb:3 and create_topic_embeds.rb:3 use `force: true`, silently dropping existing tables and data; editing already-shipped migrations is a red flag
records.rationale: The diff explicitly modifies create_top_topics.rb to add `force: true` (`create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`) and creates topic_embeds with `force: true`. `force: true` causes create_table to silently DROP an existing table before recreating it, so any deployed instance already having these tables would lose all top_topics data on upgrade. Editing a previously shipped migration is verifiable in the diff and constitutes a real data-loss defect mechanism.

records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:35 stores feed item HTML unescaped as `raw_html`, so any script or event handler in a third-party feed executes for every user; Readability whitelist in `import_remote` also permits `javascript:` URLs
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import with unfiltered feed content (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)), which creates posts with cook_method raw_html; Post#cook then 'return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]', bypassing sanitization, and embed/best.html.erb renders '<%= raw post.cooked %>'. Readability in import_remote whitelists only tags/attributes, not URL schemes, so javascript: hrefs survive absolutize_urls (which only rewrites paths starting with '/'). No contradicting detail exists in the diff.

records.issue_text: post.rb:133 lets any user who can edit a `raw_html` post submit arbitrary unsanitized HTML via the normal edit UI since `PostRevisor` preserves `cook_method`
records.rationale: The diff introduces Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] where cook() returns `raw` unsanitized (app/models/post.rb), and TopicEmbed creates posts with that cook_method. The PostRevisor changes (lib/post_revisor.rb) show revise! accepting new raw content while never touching cook_method, so a subsequent edit of such a post re-cooks as raw unsanitized HTML and updates `cooked` with it. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff; whether it's exploitable through the normal edit UI depends on edit permissions (typically author/staff for the embed user's posts), so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates `url` unescaped into an `<a href>` tag; a crafted URL passing the host check yields stored XSS in a `raw_html` post

A URL containing a single quote or event-handler payload passes the regex, yielding stored XSS. Mechanism fully visible in the diff.
